Chapter 13. The Power of Forgiveness: Letting Go of Anger.
You know, anger’s one of those emotions that shows up when we’re hurting. It’s almost like a shield—protecting us, but sometimes weighing us down more than we realize.
Imagine this boy, carrying around so much anger. He’s mad at his mother for leaving, frustrated with a system that let him down, and even blames himself for not being able to fix everything. That kind of pain? It’s raw. It can feel overwhelming, and there are days when it threatens to swallow him whole.
Sometimes, that anger just boils over—maybe it’s an argument with a foster sibling, a fight at school, or even snapping at someone who’s just trying to help. Afterward, he’s left with guilt and shame, wondering why he can’t keep it together. But here’s something a lot of people miss: anger often covers up deeper feelings, like sadness or fear. It’s so much easier to be angry than to feel vulnerable.
Over time, though, the boy starts to see that holding onto all that anger only makes his life harder. He begins to get curious about forgiveness—not as a way to say what happened was okay, but as a way to finally set himself free from what’s behind him.
It’s not easy. Forgiveness isn’t just a moment—it’s a journey, full of stops and starts, doubts and second-guessing. But with some caring adults by his side, he slowly begins to let go of some of that resentment.
Here’s the thing: forgiveness doesn’t mean forgetting, or pretending that nothing bad happened. It doesn’t mean saying what someone did was right. What it really means is choosing—again and again—not to let anger be the thing that shapes your story.
Step by step, the boy discovers that forgiveness is less about others and more about himself. It’s a way to lighten the load, to open the door to new possibilities, and to start healing for real.
